sanskrit_verse:
ये तु तिष्ठन्ति करणे तेषां सभ्यैर् विभावना ।
कथयित्वोत्तरं सम्यग् दातव्यैकस्य वादिनः ॥
transliteration: ye tu tiṣṭhanti karaṇe teṣām sabhyair vibhāvanā / kathayitvottaraṃ samyag dātavyaikasya vādinaḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: Those who stand in capacity for action must be examined by the assembly; having declared their reply correctly, the responsibility of one disputant alone is to be assigned.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in demonstrated capacity, not mere presence
Causation arises through conscious engagement and response
Restoration occurs when correct understanding is declared and validated
Consciousness alignment is achieved through clarity of assertion and acceptance
executable_legal_axioms: IF a participant stands in a case without capacity demonstration THEN exclude from active adjudication
IF a disputant provides a complete and truthful response THEN assign sole responsibility to that agent
IF multiple agents claim standing THEN evaluate each via assembly-certified inquiry protocol
IF response aligns with pramāṇa THEN recognize as valid basis for restorative process
IF no clear responder emerges THEN invoke Nyaya-guided inquiry until capacity manifests
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court proceedings, only those who demonstrate clear causal agency and articulate precise responses shall bear recognized legal weight. The court must ensure that all parties claiming relevance undergo verification of capacity before deliberation proceeds. Sole responsibility must devolve upon the one whose reply aligns with truth and completeness.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality ensures that only those capable of knowing and responding are held responsible. Anupūrvaśaḥ affirms sequential manifestation—truth spoken leads to rightful assignment. Responsibility is proportional to clarity expressed. There is no punishment here—only recognition of who holds the thread of resolution.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Vibhāvanā (assembly-based inquiry) to confirm standing
Require full Uttara (response) under witness of Dharma Sabha
Assign Ekasya Vādinaḥ Dāya (responsibility of the single speaker)
Facilitate completion through guided self-realization of role
Reintegrate integrity by affirming individual's conscious ownership of consequence
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law. Dharma is restored through recognition of capacity and truth-speaking. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
